text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov vetoed an amendment to the electoral law approved by the outgoing aprliament, which would have lowered the barrier for parties to enter parliament to three percent from four percent of the vote. @

-- Bulgarian customs officers seized six kg of heroin, hidden in a bus transiting from Turkey to Macedonia at the Kapitan Andreevo check point on the border with Turkey. One Macedonian was arrested on charges of drugs smuggling.

-- Bulgaria's biggest Confederation of Independent Trade Unions (CITU) is expected to propose to the interim government to guarantee a $40 average monthly salary to protect incomes from high inflation, CITU leader Krastyo Petkov said.
-- The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) would insist on a referendum on Bulgaria's full NATO membership, BSP leader Georgi Parvanov said. @
The caretaker government on Monday adopted a declaration stating a desire for full NATO membership.

-- Bulgaria's Interior Ministry will launch investigation into the incomes of former state officials to see whether there have been cases of misappropriation and the first results are expected in 10 days, Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said.

-- Bulgaria's interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski discussed with World Bank's resident representative Alberto Musalem the funding of Bulgaria's domestic debt and the privatisation of major Bulgarian companies. @

-- The Bulgarian fuel crisis is expected to ease in the next few days as suppliers are expected to free volumes in storage following a drastic hike of fuel prices by 176-178 percent from Tuesday, Transport minister Wilhelm Kraus said.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet is expected to offer for privatisation a bigger stake in the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company than the 25 percent equity earmarked for sell-off so far, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet is expected to offer for privatisation the state carrier Balkan Airlines, Transport minister Wilhelm Kraus said.

-- The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) may organise protests and human chains around the country against reshuffles in the management of major Bulgarian companies by the interim cabinet, BSP leader Georgi Parvanov said.
-- Monthly inflation in Bulgaria is expected to top 100 percent in February, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences' Economics Institute preliminary figures showed. @
